answer: Marking a custom state as finished (via `done = true` in `taskState.define`) only affects whether the `Task: Remove Completed` command treats it as "done." The `done` option is otherwise used mainly for code completion, and completing tasks doesn't automatically change any attribute on the containing page.

Memory for: When I define my own task state like IN PROGRESS, what does marking it as finished actually affect?
[1] Task.md (Custom states)
  Custom states: Tasks support the default `x` and ` ` states (done and not done), but custom states as well. Support for this is still basic, however. / Example: / * [NOT STARTED] Choose a photo-walk route / * [IN PROGRESS] Charge camera battery / Restrictions: / * Task states cannot contain `:` to avoid ambiguity with [[Attribute]] syntax. / To define custom states explicitly (and get code completion for them), use the [[API/taskState]] API.
  The task notation syntax is a [[Markdown]] extension to write down tasks. / Its most basic form is: / * [ ] This is my first task / which renders as follows: / * [ ] This is my first task / In a writable space, click a checkbox to change whether the task is complete. Checkboxes in these read-only docs cannot be changed.
[2] API/taskState.md (API)
  taskState.define(def): Defines a custom task state. Options: / * `name`: name of the state / * `done`: whether or not the state should be considered “done” or not, used by the `Task: Remove Completed` command / Primarily used to offer code completion for custom task states for now.
  Example: Install these definitions in a `space-lua` block in your own space and reload them: / ```lua / taskState.define { / name = "TO DO" / } / taskState.define { / name = "IN PROGRESS" / } / taskState.define { / name = "DONE", / done = true / } / ``` / Use: / * [TO DO] Still to do / * [DONE] Task already completed
[3] Markdown/Basics.md (Basic markup)
  Lists and tasks: When you click the checkbox, it will toggle its state and replace the ` ` inside the box with `x`. SilverBullet also supports custom task statuses by putting text in between `[` and `]`. When you click on such custom task states, it cycles through the states configured in your space using [[API/taskState]]. See [[Task#Custom states]]: / * [IN PROGRESS] This task is in progress / * [DONE] This task is done / * [TO DO] This task is still to be done
[4] Guide/Task Management.md (Write tasks where they belong)
  Write tasks where they belong: Add a task to the page where its context is described. Type `* [ ]` followed by the task text, or use `/task` on a line. Click its checkbox to complete it. [[Task]] explains task states and editing commands. / A page’s status is separate from task completion. Completing every task does not automatically change an attribute on the containing page.
[5] Tag/data.md (data)
  Defining your own root tags: Use a hashtag as the block’s language, and every object in it gets that name as its [[Tag#Root tags|root tag]]. This is how you define a new kind of object in plain Markdown: / ```#contact / $ref: pete-contact / name: Pete / age: 55 / ``` / These objects can be queried via the `contact` tag: / ${query[[from index.objects("contact")]]} / Built-in tag names are taken: a ` ```#task ` block would look like a real task, so it is not indexed, and lint flags it.
